text.p: A privatisation offer of two million shares in Amriyah Cement was oversubscribed but the state holding company which owns the shares has not yet decided how to allocate them, an agent said on Wednesday.

An official of the National Bank of Egypt, one of the two agents for the sale, said the state's Holding Company for Metallurgical Industries received 38 applications for shares, in some cases several from the same strategic investor. The offer was limited to big investors.
"They amount to more than two million but I don't have the exact figure," the official said. "They haven't decided when the sale will take place or how to allocate the shares."
The deadline for applications for the shares -- 10 percent of the equity of Amriyah Cement -- was last Monday afternoon.
Private investors and funds own 34.6 percent of Amriyah and the holding company holds the remaining 65.4 percent.
The shares last traded on the Egyptian stock exchange at 70.50 pounds, giving the company a valuation of 1.41 billion pounds ($415 million).
The new shareholders will be entitled to a cash dividend of 5.25 pounds per share for the financial year 1995/6, which ended last June 30.
In late November, Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid said Egypt had rejected a bid for a strategic stake in Amriyah Cement from French firm Lafarge because it was the only competitor.
